subject: HelixPay pilot: request to pin model + regional residency (no-fallback)
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya@helixpay.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: pin model + region residency for HelixPay pilot

Hi Grace —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are ready to move forward with a small pilot (payment dispute summarization) but legal and compliance have a hard requirement: inference must be performed in the US-only (no cross-border fallbacks) and the model used must be the vetted, engineered variant we evaluated during the POC. They explicitly banned automatic fallback to alternate models or regional replicas.

Can Redwood support a 1) forced model pin (no automatic fallback), 2) region lock to us-east-2, and 3) an SLO/telemetry contract for audit logs?

Pilot asks:
- Duration: 8 weeks, start target Oct 4
- Volume: ~300k tokens/month initially (ramp to 700k)
- Success metrics: latency p95 < 350ms, accuracy on labeled set > 92%

I attached the official request form and traffic estimate. We know this increases risk/cost on your side; HelixPay will sign a short SOW and cover a portion of the delta if needed.

Let me know the technical blockers and an ETA for a decision.

—Priya
Priya Rao

On Fri, Sep 18, 2026 at 11:06 AM Grace O'Connor <grace@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding HelixPay's ask. Bottom line: they want a strict no-fallback, region-locked, forced model pin for their pilot.

We can do this but there are tradeoffs and operational constraints to call out up front:

1) Architecture: we will create a dedicated routing policy for the HelixPay tenant that pins calls to the provisioned model variant (recommended: rwdw-legal-3b-q4 — the variant we vetted). Fallbacks will be explicitly disabled at the routing layer.

2) Cache/Batching: with no-fallback we lose some cross-model cache reuse; expect higher token cost per inference. We'll enable prefix caching only within the pinned model.

3) Telemetry & audit: we can stream request/response hashes + full audit logs to the contract S3 bucket (30 day retention by default; can extend). We will add a route-level trace_id and tie it to HelixPay's account id for audits.

4) Canary/rollback plan (attached runbook):
   - Canary cluster in us-east-2 with 10% of traffic for 72 hours (manual promotion).
   - Monitors: error rate, latency p95, degraded-quality alerts from evals on reserved prompt set.
   - Rollback triggers: error spike > 3x baseline, latency p95 > 500ms for > 30m, or quality metric drop > 5% on labeled prompts.

5) Required lead time & dependencies: need 10 business days to provision and validate the canary (includes infra capacity and model quantization checks).

Attachments: canary-runbook.md, traffic-estimates.xlsx

If HelixPay insists on immediate hard lock without canary we'll need an explicit sign-off acknowledging increased risk and a temporary premium to offset lost multiplexing/caching.

—Karthik
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: RE: Request: pin model + region residency for HelixPay pilot

Grace / team — quick ops note on cost & capacity.

- Cost impact: hard pin + region lock (us-east-2) will increase per-token cost roughly ~38–45% versus the default routed configuration (depends on real utilization). The lack of fallback misses opportunistic batching on lower-cost variants.
- Capacity: us-east-2 has spare capacity for this pilot but we need to reserve a burst buffer for week 1 (recommend reserve 2x expected baseline for 72 hours).
- Runbook: canary plan is fine. Ops can provision a dedicated nodepool and monitoring dashboards. We'll surface a one-time provisioning estimate by EOD tomorrow.

If HelixPay will accept the canary + rollback conditions, ops can proceed without a permanent surcharge for long-term runs (we can amortize provisioning cost into usage). If they want immediate hard-lock to prod, we should bill a temporary premium during the first 30 days.

—Marcus
Head of Dedicated Capacity & Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwoodinference.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, marcus_lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 14:37:00 -04:00
Subject: Decision & next steps: HelixPay pilot (pin + regional residency)

Priya / team —

Thanks for the form. After reviewing technical and ops feedback, Product and Legal approve the pilot under the following conditions (final sign-off contingent on SOW signature by both parties):

1) Canary: 72-hour canary in us-east-2 with 10% traffic. Manual promotion to 100% only if rollback triggers are not met.
2) Hard-pin allowed after successful canary. Prior to hard-pin we will keep fallback disabled by policy but not forcibly block emergency-rollback channels for ops (ops retains the ability to direct-traffic to a pre-agreed standby variant in extreme incidents).
3) Auditing: Redwood will provide request/response hashes and per-request trace_ids to HelixPay's contract S3 bucket. Retention: 90 days for pilot (extendable).
4) Usage cap: Pilot capped at 700k tokens/month. Any overage billed per agreed SOW rates.
5) Billing: HelixPay will accept a configuration premium for the first 30 days equal to estimated delta in per-token cost (we'll send the number tomorrow).

Grace, Karthik, Marcus — please send the final provisioning estimate and attach the canary runbook and SOW draft. Priya — I'll loop in GTM for billing and the SOW.

Priya — welcome aboard. We'll schedule a kick-off for Oct 1 to validate telemetry and run the canary checklist.

—Lauren
VP Product (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
